justification: Corrects DQ-69's tracker headline (which said '67 days blind, schedule not repaired' three weeks after both root causes were actually fixed) and splits out a genuinely separate, still-open defect (7 SEPP/LEP instruments unactioned on needs_review) as a new row, DQ-88, with its own real probe. Standard tier because it adds a new query-backed check to scripts/dq_probe_live.py, not just prose -- Minor would undersell that.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/dq_check.py && python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-69 && python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-88
falsifiable_check.fails_when: the tracker's declared status disagrees with dq_checks.json's declared field for either row (dq_check.py's own cross-source check), or either probe's count regresses from what this commit measured (DQ-69: 1, DQ-88: 7).
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Forced red twice while building this: (1) added DQ-88 with check:[] -> 'a row was added without a check that can fail', cap ratchets correctly refused it; (2) wrote DQ-69's tracker status as an unqualified checkmark while dq_checks.json still declared it open -> 'the ledger and the check file declare different statuses', dq_check.py's own cross-source consistency check caught it. Both fixed by writing a real DQ-88 probe and matching DQ-69's status-column convention to its actual declared state (open, with a named residual) rather than a bare checkmark. Final state: dq_check.py PASSED, 45 checks/93 rows/0 red.

pre_impl.existing_data: instrument_registry (26 active rows) -- read-only throughout, verified via dq_db.py's read-only session before writing anything. DQ-69's query and DQ-88's query were both re-run live against production before being written into either the tracker or the probe file.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed initially that DQ-69's own probe (dq_checks.json note) and the DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md headline would agree once re-measured -- they did not: the JSON note already recorded both root causes fixed and predicted a floor of 1, dated from whenever the fix landed, while the tracker's human-facing headline was never updated and still described the pre-fix state. This is the exact 'check knew, prose didn't' pattern this branch's own earlier DQ-79 fix (same session) described.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: DQ-69's declared status is left as 'open' (not flipped to 'fixed') because its probe is a strict count==0 test and will never pass while Wingecarribee lacks a pco_instrument_id -- declaring it fixed would immediately recreate the declared-fixed-but-red mismatch this exact commit is correcting elsewhere. DQ-88 is a wholly new row, not a rename of anything existing.

functions.name: PROBES['DQ-88'] (registered in scripts/dq_probe_live.py, dispatched by main())
functions.input: no CLI args beyond --id DQ-88; reads instrument_registry via the shared read-only dq_db session
functions.output: prints count + query + explanation to stdout, exits 1 if count > 0 else 0 -- same dispatch shape as every other entry in PROBES, unmodified
functions.if_none: if instrument_registry.needs_review is somehow NULL rather than a boolean, the WHERE clause's implicit boolean-true test simply excludes it -- schema declares the column boolean not-null, so this is not a live path

values.guard_at: WHERE is_active AND needs_review, no null-handling needed

values.read_at: scripts/dq_probe_live.py DQ-69 entry (pre-existing, unchanged by this commit)
values.nullable: yes -- NULL means never checked, handled explicitly in the WHERE clause
values.guard_at: WHERE ... last_checked IS NULL OR last_checked < NOW() - INTERVAL '14 days'
values.if_missing: counted as stale (correct -- never-checked is the worst case, not an exemption)

queries.purpose: confirm DQ-69's residual is unchanged (still exactly the documented floor) and identify DQ-88's 7 instruments by name before writing either row
queries.file_line: ad-hoc read-only queries via scripts/dq_db.py, mirroring dq_probe_live.py's own DQ-69/DQ-88 SQL
queries.where_clause: instrument_registry WHERE is_active AND (last_checked IS NULL OR needs_review), ordered by needs_review DESC, last_checked NULLS FIRST
queries.if_zero: would mean both defects had already cleared themselves -- not the case, 8 rows returned (1 never-checked + 7 needs_review)
queries.if_wrong: cross-checked against the ops Telegram alert log's independent timestamps (14/08, 21/08, 28/08 runs) and against dq_checks.json's own pre-existing note, which already predicted a floor of 1 for DQ-69 -- three independent sources agree

break_it.scenario: DQ-88's check is read as proof that the 7 flagged instruments are current, when it only proves the backlog count.
break_it.what_happens: A green DQ-88 run could be misread as 'all SEPP/LEP data is verified', when someone could have cleared a flag without reading the underlying change.
break_it.how: The dq_checks.json note explicitly states this limitation: 'this check counts the backlog, not correctness ... a green run here is not proof any given instrument is current, only that the visible backlog is empty.'
break_it.repro: read the note field directly; no code enforces this since it is a documentation limitation, not a technical one

break_it.scenario: DQ-69's residual (1, Wingecarribee) is mistaken for a new defect on a future re-read, triggering wasted investigation.
break_it.what_happens: Someone re-derives 'why is this 1 and not 0' from scratch instead of reading the already-recorded reason.
break_it.how: Both the tracker row and dq_checks.json's passes_when field state explicitly that 1 is the documented, expected floor (wingecarribee_lep_2010 has no pco_instrument_id) and that 0 requires giving it one -- a deliberate follow-up, not a mystery.

break_it.scenario: DQ-88 double-counts or overlaps with DQ-69, corrupting the DQ-CHECK row/check totals.
break_it.what_happens: The two rows measure genuinely different populations and neither's fix affects the other.
break_it.how: DQ-69 counts by last_checked staleness; DQ-88 counts by needs_review flag. Verified they are disjoint concerns: all 7 needs_review rows in this measurement have check_failures=0 and were checked at the same recent timestamp as the healthy majority -- none of them are also stale by DQ-69's definition.
break_it.repro: instrument_registry WHERE needs_review AND (last_checked IS NULL OR last_checked < NOW() - INTERVAL '14 days') returns 0

post_merge.manual_verify: The actual substantive follow-up (opening each of the 7 needs_review instruments and clearing or applying what the monitor flagged) is explicitly NOT done here -- it is judgement work per instrument, tracked as the open DQ-88 backlog this commit creates, not resolved by it.
